title: Maximize the Topmost Element After K Moves
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, where nums[0] represents the topmost element of the pile, you are allowed to make exactly k moves.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, where nums[0] represents the topmost element of the pile, you are allowed to make exactly k moves. Each move can consist of either removing the topmost element of the pile or adding any previously removed element back onto the pile. The objective is to achieve the maximum possible value for the topmost element after performing these k moves. If it is not possible to maintain a non-empty pile after k moves, return -1.
constraints: The first list element is the pile top.
Each of exactly k moves either removes the current top or returns one previously removed value to the top.
Return the greatest achievable top value, or -1 when every exact-k outcome is empty.
hints: After k moves, candidates are values removed during the first k-1 moves or the untouched value at index k.
Handle the one-element parity trap, then inspect exactly those reachable candidates.
For n>1 take max(nums[:k-1]) and also nums[k] when in range; special-case k=0 and n=1.
Any earlier removed value can be restored on the last move, while reaching nums[k] uses all k removals; no other value can be top in exactly k moves.
editorial: Any earlier removed value can be restored on the last move, while reaching nums[k] uses all k removals; no other value can be top in exactly k moves.

tests.explanation: Remove up to three candidates and return five on move four; no larger reachable top exists.
The sole value must be removed and nothing can be returned during the same move, leaving an empty pile.
